images.title: 2 l 50 ml and 2,500 ml on a number line
images.purpose: Show that once both capacities are in ml they can be compared as numbers: 2 l 50 ml is 2,050 ml, which is less than 2,500 ml.
images.composition: One number line in ml with two marked points, the capacity in l and ml joined to its ml, and the comparison written below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. NUMBER LINE: one thin dark #1F2937 horizontal line at y 400 from x 150 to x 1306 representing 2,000 ml to 2,600 ml (1.93 px per ml), with four tall tick marks (44 px) at x 150, 535, 921 and 1306 labelled under the line 2,000 ml, 2,200 ml, 2,400 ml and 2,600 ml (36 px, dark, y 470). POINT A: a teal #0072B2 dot (28 px) on the line at x 246 with the label 2,050 ml above it (44 px, bold, teal) in a rounded rectangle 260 by 64 px at y 290 to 354, and under it at y 560 a tag 2 l 50 ml (40 px, bold) joined to the dot by a thin grey #6B7280 line with an equals sign (=) in the middle. POINT B: an amber #E69F00 dot (28 px) on the line at x 1113 with the label 2,500 ml above it (44 px, bold, amber-dark) in a rounded rectangle 260 by 64 px at y 290 to 354. RESULT at the bottom centre, y 700: the text 2,050 < 2,500 (72 px, bold, dark #1F2937). Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of tick marks that differs from 4
a point that is not at 2,050 or 2,500
the comparison sign pointing the wrong way
images.takeaway: Change both capacities to ml, then the smaller number is the smaller capacity: 2 l 50 ml < 2,500 ml.
images.description: A number line in ml with 2,050 ml and 2,500 ml marked, 2 l 50 ml joined to 2,050 ml, and 2,050 < 2,500.
images.context: Concept image for Comparing Capacities. It follows the idea of comparing quantities in your maths book and shows the concept's own example (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Ask which point is further along the line. The slip to watch: comparing 2 and 2,500 without a common unit.

image_decisions.why: Both capacities on one line in one unit make the comparison a matter of position.
